name: Dark Green Blue
lede: Dark Green Blue is a deep teal, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[green-blue]], recorded only in the xkcd color survey of 2010.

sections.title: A darkened green-blue
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[green-blue]] [1]. Unlike many of the library's darkened shades, it carries no Ridgway or ISCC-NBS filing; its only source is the crowd-sourced xkcd color survey of 2010, so the boundary between this swatch and its neighbors rests on informal usage rather than an official dictionary [1]. On a monitor it sits closer to teal than to either pure green or pure blue [1].

The closest named neighbors on file are [[opal-green]] and [[pearl-opal-green]], both close enough to be mistaken for it, with [[runnymede]] a touch greener [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 20 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.08 per cent, as photographed [2]. It plays a shadow role more often than a mid-tone, is rare before 1900, and is markedly over-represented among Post-Impressionist paintings in our sample [2]. France shows the largest raw count of matches, though at a rate close to the archive's overall average, so its presence there is mostly a matter of sample size rather than special favor [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
